rows.requirement: The platform MUST maintain approved, versioned red-flag rule packs by age group and pregnancy status. Rule execution precedes the LLM response.
rows.note: Versioned packs; rules run before any model call.

rows.requirement: A red flag MUST create an immutable risk event, urgent case, recommended action, configured destination and escalation timer.
rows.note: Red flag opens an emergency case with an SLA clock.

rows.requirement: The LLM MUST NOT downgrade a deterministic urgent classification. Only an authorised clinician can override it, with reason and audit.
rows.note: Severity is raise-only; only a clinician override lowers it.

rows.requirement: When location or referral data is unavailable, the system MUST state that limitation and give the nationally approved fallback instruction.
rows.note: Says it does not know the facility rather than inventing one.

rows.requirement: The response MUST use action-first language: what to do now, what not to delay, where to seek help and what information to take.
rows.note: Outcome text is action-first.

rows.requirement: Advice MUST be conditioned on crop or animal type, growth/age stage, approximate location, season/date, observed symptoms, affected proportion, recent inputs/treatments and available evidence.
The system MUST distinguish observation from confirmed diagnosis. Visual classification outputs are “possible matches” until evidence and confidence thresholds are met.
rows.note: Candidates stay possible matches below the threshold.

rows.requirement: Chemical recommendations require an approved product registry, local authorisation status, label-derived instructions, protective-equipment warning and pre-harvest/re-entry information where applicable. If registry verification fails, the system MUST not invent a product or rate.
rows.note: No registry match means no product and no rate.

rows.requirement: Advice SHOULD prioritise feasible, low-cost integrated pest-management actions and explicitly flag actions that could harm people, animals, crops, soil or water.
Market prices MUST display source, market, unit, grade/quality where known, observation timestamp and staleness. The assistant must never represent stale or unverified prices as live offers.
rows.note: Source, market, unit, date and staleness on every price.

rows.requirement: The platform MUST store an age/grade band and preferred language, not infer sensitive traits from voice.
Adaptation MUST use demonstrated mastery, requested difficulty, response history and educator configuration. It MUST NOT label a child as unintelligent or diagnose a learning disability.
rows.note: No permanent aptitude label; tested adversarially.

rows.requirement: The tutor MUST use a “teach, check, adapt” loop: explain one concept, ask a short comprehension check, assess the answer against a rubric, then remediate or progress.
rows.note: Teach, check, adapt.

rows.requirement: For assessed homework, the tutor SHOULD provide hints and reasoning before a final answer and must identify when content may be copied rather than understood.
Child-facing conversations MUST apply age-appropriate content filters, privacy minimisation, abuse/self-harm escalation and restrictions on commercial persuasion.
rows.note: Age filters and safeguarding, including grooming.

rows.requirement: Citizens MAY use anonymous or pseudonymous sessions where service policy permits. Phone verification cannot be the only access route.
rows.note: Anonymous citizen sessions.

rows.requirement: Staff use federated identity where available, MFA and role plus attribute-based access.
rows.note: RBAC, ABAC, MFA and OIDC federation with signature, issuer, audience, nonce and domain checks. A staff account is never auto-provisioned from a token.

rows.requirement: Sensitive exports, clinical overrides, rule publication and break-glass access require step-up authentication.
Break-glass access expires automatically, requires justification and alerts the data protection/safety owner.
Role changes revoke active sessions and queued export links according to policy.
rows.note: Session epoch withdraws tokens on role change.

rows.requirement: Consent is purpose-specific: service delivery, follow-up contact, precise location, analytics, research/model improvement and cross-programme referral are separate choices.
Consent scripts are delivered in the selected language and channel and record script version plus affirmative action.
rows.note: Script version and language recorded with the act.

rows.requirement: Withdrawal stops future optional processing but preserves records required by lawful retention; the user receives a plain-language explanation.
Proxy/caregiver relationships record who is present, on whose behalf and the authority/assent basis.
rows.note: Records on whose behalf and the basis.

rows.requirement: Queues support domain, geography, service point, risk, skill, language and workload routing.
Assignment is atomic and prevents two workers unknowingly owning the same case.
Notes support structured fields and append-only narrative entries; edits create new versions.
rows.note: Notes are insert-only.

rows.requirement: SLA timers pause only for configured reasons and every pause is audited.
Merge and duplicate resolution preserve all source identifiers and events.
Closure requires outcome, action taken, citizen reachability and follow-up decision.
Templates are versioned by language, channel, domain, risk and sensitivity.
Delivery attempts, provider IDs, consent, quiet hours, failures and retries are recorded.
Urgent alerts use an escalation policy with acknowledgement; a sent message is not treated as acknowledged.
rows.note: Sent is not acknowledged.

rows.requirement: Lock-screen/SMS text uses privacy-safe wording.
Broadcasts require audience estimate, duplicate suppression, approval, rate controls and opt-out compliance.
Availability 99.5% pilot; 99.9% national core monthly, excluding approved maintenance
rows.note: An availability percentage is a property of the deployment and its operations, not of the repository.

rows.requirement: Voice responsiveness P95 first acknowledgement <2s online; P95 useful response <12s text path and <20s voice path, excluding long uploads
rows.note: The objective is defined and measured: p95 per turn, with fewer than 30 observations reported as unmeasured rather than met. The number itself is a property of a running deployment.

rows.requirement: Urgent rule execution P99 deterministic danger-rule result <2s after transcript/structured input availability
rows.note: Rules are pure functions with no model call.

rows.requirement: Durability Accepted case/event loss RPO <=5 minutes; critical configuration RPO <=1 minute
rows.note: The recovery point objective is a database replication and backup configuration.

rows.requirement: Recovery Core service RTO <=60 minutes pilot and <=30 minutes national target
rows.note: The recovery time objective is proven by a restore exercise, which has not been run.

rows.requirement: Scale Horizontal scaling tested to 10x forecast peak; per-channel backpressure and admission control
rows.note: The application scales horizontally by construction. Load testing to ten times peak has not been run.

rows.requirement: Offline 72 hours of field capture and at least 200 queued events per managed device without data loss
rows.note: Two hundred events captured across seventy-two hours, replayed in the order spoken, each exactly once, nothing discarded when the sync drops halfway. Device storage quota remains a handset property.

rows.requirement: Accessibility WCAG 2.2 AA for PWA/staff portals plus voice-specific usability testing
rows.note: WCAG 2.2 A/AA checked by axe-core on all 37 pages, zero violations, failing the run on one. The voice-specific usability testing the target also names is fieldwork with citizens.

rows.requirement: Observability 100% requests traceable across adapter, workflow, model/tool and persistence by trace ID
Maintainability >=80% unit coverage for deterministic domain/policy code; 100% rule coverage for safety rule packs
rows.note: 80 % thresholds enforced on the deterministic domain and policy code, and every safety rule proven individually reachable.

rows.requirement: Compatibility Android baseline selected from pilot device survey; last two major evergreen desktop browsers
rows.note: The Android baseline is chosen from a pilot device survey, which has not been run.

rows.requirement: Localisation No production string outside localisation registry; fallback and untranslated-string telemetry
Tenancy and access Automated tests prove row/object isolation across tenants and roles
Consent and citizen session User completes, refuses and withdraws each purpose in supported language
Voice/media ingestion Resumable, checked, encrypted upload survives disconnect and duplicate submission
rows.note: Resumable, checksummed, encrypted.

rows.requirement: Language pipeline Code-switched utterance returns span-aware transcript with uncertainty and correction
Orchestration Replayable workflow calls typed tools, times out safely and records exact versions
Health vertical Deterministic red flag escalates independently of LLM and reaches acknowledged human queue
Agriculture vertical Guided image capture yields evidence-aware candidates and safe constrained action
Education vertical Offline teach-check-adapt session syncs once and records topic evidence
Case management Assignment, SLA, transition, override, merge and closure are permissioned and audited
Knowledge governance Reviewed content publishes with validity and is the only production retrieval source
Notifications Sensitive templates, delivery/acknowledgement, retries and escalation are observable
Dashboards Metrics expose definition/freshness and suppress unsafe small cells
MLOps/evaluation Versioned release fails automatically when a safety/language threshold regresses
rows.note: Language gates, the adversarial suite and canary rollout at 5 % held for seven days.

rows.requirement: Security/operations Incident, backup restore, provider failure and key rotation are exercised successfully
rows.note: Controls are built and scanned in CI. Backup restore, provider failure and key rotation are exercises against a running deployment; docs/SECURITY.md names the key-rotation hazard.

rows.requirement: A citizen calling the national short code hears a greeting in a rotating order of the five languages within 6 seconds and can say or press the language; language is remembered by caller ID for future calls.
After language selection the system asks one open question ("Tell me what you need — health, farming or school") and routes by intent; a DTMF fallback (1/2/3) is always available.
Audio is captured in 8 kHz AMR-NB/G.711 and streamed to the STT service; end-of-utterance detection ≤ 800 ms silence; barge-in supported.
rows.note: Barge-in and the configured end-of-utterance silence, sent as whole seconds because the gateway refuses a fraction. The codec is negotiated by the trunk.

rows.requirement: Each AI reply ≤ 25 seconds of speech; longer content is chunked with "shall I continue?".
Calls are toll-free to the citizen (reverse-billed to the programme) — commercial arrangement with MNOs is a programme dependency (Risk R-03).
rows.note: Reverse billing so the citizen pays nothing is a commercial arrangement with the mobile operators.

rows.requirement: If the call drops, the session is resumable for 24 hours by calling back from the same number; the system summarises where it left off.
Emergency phrase detection ("il ne respire plus", "azali kokoka te", etc.) short-circuits the flow to the emergency script and CHW alert within 3 seconds.
rows.note: Deterministic, before any model call.

rows.requirement: Voice notes (OGG/Opus) are accepted and transcribed; replies are returned as both a voice note and text in the user's language.
Photos and short videos (≤ 30 s, ≤ 16 MB) are accepted for the Agriculture module; the system asks for a second angle if the first is low-confidence.
Interactive buttons (max 3) and list messages (max 10) are used for confirmations; never free-text-only when a choice is needed.
24-hour session window rules of the WhatsApp platform are respected; proactive follow-ups use approved template messages.
Opt-in and opt-out ("STOP"/"ARRÊT"/"TIKA") handled in all five languages.
USSD offers a 2-level menu: module → 5 most common questions per module → SMS answer in the user's language (≤ 3 concatenated SMS).
USSD sessions ≤ 180 s (gateway limit); state persisted so the citizen can dial again.
SMS is the delivery channel for reminders (vaccination, planting, revision) and follow-ups; each includes a callback short code.
Next.js 14 App Router PWA, installable, offline shell cached, IndexedDB queue for outgoing voice notes/photos when offline, background sync on reconnect.
Push-to-talk UI with a single large button; text remains secondary; every screen reachable in ≤ 2 taps.
Worker PWA (CHW/Extension/Teacher) shares the same shell with role-gated routes.
citizen_id is a platform UUID; phone number, WhatsApp ID and PWA account are identifiers linked to it. Merging identifiers requires citizen confirmation by voice OTP.
rows.note: One citizen across IVR, SMS, USSD and WhatsApp, and a spoken one-time code with a ten-minute life and three attempts before an identifier is added.

rows.requirement: Because phones are shared, each session opens with a lightweight confirmation ("Is this still Maman Nsimba? Say yes or no") when the last session was for a different named profile; anonymous sessions are permitted.
Language ID returns top-2 languages with probabilities; if top-1 < 0.70, the system asks the user to confirm ("Lingala to?").
STT returns word-level timestamps and per-segment confidence; segments < 0.55 confidence trigger a targeted re-ask ("I heard 'fever for 3 days' — is that right?").
rows.note: Element-level confirmation. Word timestamps are not returned by every provider.

rows.requirement: Mixed-language utterances are handled without forcing the user to choose; token language tags are stored.
Every reply is generated in French canonical form first, then rendered in the user's language. Canonical French is stored for audit and for human workers.
rows.note: French canonical, stored for the worker.

rows.requirement: A per-domain terminology glossary (e.g., "malaria" → Lingala "malaria/ndese", "fertiliser" → …) is enforced in translation via constrained decoding/post-edit; glossaries are versioned and editable by admins (§15).
Simplification: target reading/listening level equivalent to end of primary school; sentence length ≤ 15 words for voice output; numerals spoken as words in local convention.
TTS voices: one female and one male per language; voice selection per module configurable; all voices reviewed by native-speaker panels for intelligibility and cultural fit.
rows.note: Two voices per language where a provider offers them.

rows.requirement: Human-recorded prompts are used for fixed scripts (greetings, emergency scripts, disclaimers) in all languages, regardless of TTS quality.
rows.note: The fixed scripts and the delivery path are built and tested; missingRecordings() reports which are unrecorded. Recording them with native speakers is studio work.

rows.requirement: The pipeline exposes transcription_confidence, translation_confidence and overall_language_confidence to the Risk Agent.

Collect ≥ 200 hours of transcribed conversational speech per low-resource language across ≥ 3 provinces, balanced by gender and age, using the health/agri/edu domains as prompts; consent captured per §16.
rows.note: Two hundred hours of transcribed speech per language is field collection with consent, not code.

rows.requirement: Build a 2,000-utterance gold evaluation set per language per module, annotated with intent, entities and severity.
rows.note: The gold evaluation sets are a content deliverable; the gates in gates.ts have nothing to read until they exist.

rows.requirement: Native-speaker linguists (2 per language) on retainer for glossary, prompt review and TTS QA.
rows.note: Two native-speaker linguists per language on retainer, for glossary, prompt review and voice quality.

rows.requirement: Data licensing: corpus is owned by the programme (FDSU/Government) with Nseya holding a perpetual licence for model improvement — [DECISION REQUIRED] contractually.
rows.note: Who owns the corpus and on what licence is a contractual decision recorded as open in the specification.

rows.requirement: A DomainResult failing schema validation is rejected and the turn falls back to a safe scripted response + low-confidence flag; the failure is an ai.contract.violation event.
rows.note: A contract violation falls back to a safe scripted answer.

rows.requirement: Max 2 clarifying questions per turn; each is a single closed or short question; after 2, the agent proceeds with stated assumptions and flags assumed=true in system_understanding.

confidence_overall = min(stt_conf, intent_conf, domain_conf) adjusted by Risk Agent; < 0.60 → response is prefixed with a caution and offers a human; < 0.40 → scripted safe answer only + case created (severity 1) for human review.

Each module has a curated, versioned knowledge base (Markdown/PDF source → chunked → embedded in a vector store) reviewed by the domain board (§17). Sources: Ministry of Health community guidelines, WHO/IMCI community materials, INERA/FAO agronomy notes for DRC crops, programme national curriculum. Every generated recommendation must cite ≥ 1 KB document ID or protocol ID; uncited health/agr

Clinical Review Board (CRB): ≥ 2 Congolese physicians + 1 community health expert approve every health protocol version, emergency script, KB document and the health system prompt; nothing health-related ships without CRB sign-off recorded in protocol_versions.approved_by.
rows.note: The approval mechanism is built and every version records its approver. Constituting the clinical review board is a governance act; until then every protocol carries "En attente du Comité de Revue Clinique".

rows.requirement: Agronomy and Pedagogy panels: analogous review for agri KB and education content.
rows.note: The approval mechanism exists for every knowledge document. Constituting agronomy and pedagogy panels is governance work.

rows.requirement: Red-team suite: ≥ 300 adversarial/edge cases per module per language (dangerous self-medication requests, pesticide misuse, exam cheating, abusive content, hallucination bait); run in CI on every prompt/model change; release blocked on any severity-4 miss.
rows.note: The gate runs in CI and blocks on any miss; 126 cases, whose first run exposed 24 real defects, now fixed. Reaching 300 per module per language is authoring work with native speakers.

rows.requirement: Grounding rule: health/agri recommendations must cite KB/protocol IDs; a recommendation without citation is replaced by a safe scripted fallback and logged.

Disclaimer policy: identity statement at session start ("I am the CVOS voice assistant, not a doctor/agronomist/teacher") — human-recorded, once per session; no repetitive disclaimers thereafter; a "talk to a person" option is always one utterance away.
rows.note: Said once per session, never repeated.

rows.requirement: Misinformation guard: Risk Agent runs a classifier on outbound text for unsupported medical/agri claims; positive hits block and route to fallback.
Uncertainty recording: every turn stores confidences and any assumptions; low-confidence turns sampled daily for human review (target 100/day in pilot).

Learning loop: overrides, feedback, follow-up outcomes and reviewer labels flow to an evaluation dataset; model/prompt changes are evaluated offline against gold sets and red-team suites, then canaried to 5% traffic for 7 days.
rows.note: Overrides, feedback and corrections feed the corpus; a change reaches citizens through a 5 % canary held for seven days.

rows.requirement: Bias & fairness: per-language and per-gender quality metrics reported monthly; a language whose metrics fall below §6.5 gates is downgraded to scripted mode automatically.
Content boundaries: no political, religious or legal advice; no financial products; abuse/threat detection routes to a safeguarding script and, where the user is a child, to the teacher/CHW path.

Triage runs on versioned decision trees (protocol_versions) authored in a YAML DSL and approved by the Clinical Review Board. Initial protocol set (MVP): fever in child < 5; fever in adult; cough/difficulty breathing; diarrhoea and dehydration; pregnancy danger signs; newborn danger signs; injury/bleeding; malnutrition screening (MUAC where available); vaccination schedule lookup; general
rows.note: Ten protocols.

rows.requirement: Each protocol defines: questions (with per-language phrasing), branching, severity output (0 self-care, 1 monitor, 2 visit clinic within 24 h, 3 visit today, 4 emergency now), recommended actions and referral text.
The LLM's role is to map free speech to protocol answers (structured extraction) and to explain the outcome; it cannot alter severity.
Any red-flag answer immediately yields severity 4 without completing the tree.
Symptom intake accepts free speech; the Health Agent extracts entities (symptom, duration, age group, pregnancy status, location) and asks only missing protocol questions.
Emergency (severity 4) → scripted emergency instructions in the user's language + nearest facility (if known) + CHW alert within 60 s + SMS to the citizen with the facility name.
Severity 2–3 → case created, assigned to the territory's CHW queue, SLA 24 h / 4 h respectively; citizen receives follow-up call/SMS at +24 h.
Vaccination reminders: citizen states child's date of birth (or age) → national EPI schedule → SMS/voice reminders; opt-in required.
Maternal health: pregnancy status captured with explicit consent; ANC visit reminders; danger-sign protocol always available.

Medication guidance limited to approved protocol text (e.g., ORS preparation, paracetamol per national community guidance if included); any other medication question → "ask a nurse/pharmacist" + optional case.
Health interaction summaries (≤ 60 words, canonical French) are generated for every turn and visible to assigned workers.
Anonymised health trend aggregation by territory/week for dashboards (§14) with k-anonymity ≥ 10.
rows.note: k-anonymity of 10.

rows.requirement: Inputs: voice/text description; up to 5 photos; ≤ 30 s video (frames extracted server-side); optional crop, growth stage, location (auto from territory profile).
Crop issue identification returns top-3 candidates with probabilities from the vision classifier; the VLM produces a plain-language description and asks for a second photo when top-1 < 0.60.
Recommendations are tiered: (a) no-cost cultural practices, (b) low-cost locally available inputs, (c) inputs requiring purchase — with a note on where to obtain via extension officer.

Notifiable pests/diseases list (configurable: fall armyworm, cassava mosaic/brown streak, banana bunchy top, Newcastle disease, PPR, etc.) triggers an extension-officer alert and contributes to cluster detection.
Cluster detection: ≥ N reports (default 5) of the same issue/crop in the same territory within 14 days → agri.cluster.detected event → extension dashboard alert + optional broadcast.

Planting calendars by province and crop (maize, cassava, rice, beans, groundnut, plantain, vegetables) maintained as KB tables; the agent answers "when" questions from these, adjusted by seasonal forecasts where available.
Weather: territory-level 5-day forecast from a provider via the gateway; rendered in plain language ("heavy rain likely Thursday — delay applying fertiliser").

Market prices: weekly price sheet per major market (Kinshasa, Lubumbashi, Kisangani, Mbuji-Mayi, Goma, Matadi …) maintained by data partners or admin upload; agent quotes date and market; never guarantees a price.
Livestock: symptom intake for poultry, goats, pigs, cattle → severity + "contact veterinary/extension" path; zoonotic red flags escalate.
Buyer opportunities (Phase 4): informational listing of cooperative/buyer contacts by commodity, admin-maintained.
rows.note: Buyer and cooperative listings are placed in Phase 4 by the specification itself, after the pilot.

rows.requirement: Learner profile: age band (6–8, 9–11, 12–14, 15–18, adult), level (primaire 1–6, secondaire 1–6/humanités), language of instruction, preferred explanation language. Profile is optional; defaults inferred conservatively from speech and confirmed.
Explain-at-level: any topic explained in ≤ 90 s of speech at the profile level, with one concrete local example (market, farming, river, football).
Read-aloud: stories and passages from a curated, licensed/open library in the five languages; Phase 3 adds TTS narration of user-uploaded photos of textbook pages (OCR → simplify → read).
rows.note: The read-aloud library is built. Narration of a photographed textbook page is placed in Phase 3 by the specification itself.

rows.requirement: Oral quiz: 5-question quizzes generated per topic; voice answers scored; results stored as learning_signals.

Homework support: step-by-step guidance; for maths, the agent works one worked example then coaches the learner through theirs; it never reads back a final answer to a graded assignment unless the learner has attempted it.
Exam prep (TENAFEP, Examen d'État) drawn from official objectives; revision plans by weeks-to-exam; SMS revision nudges.
Parent mode: explain what the child is studying and how to help without literacy.
Teacher mode (worker PWA): class-level learning-gap view; ready-made oral quizzes; broadcast of revision reminders.
Difficulty tracking: repeated failures on a concept produce learning_gap signals aggregated by school/territory.
Reuse of StudYear AI-OS components (quiz generation, spaced-repetition scheduling, curriculum graph) through a shared internal package — [DECISION REQUIRED] on package boundary with StudYear.
rows.note: The shared-package boundary with StudYear is an open commercial decision in the specification itself.

rows.requirement: Cases are created automatically for severity ≥ 2, low confidence < 0.40, notifiable agri issues, and any citizen explicit request for a human.

Assignment routing: territory → org → role → availability (worker "on duty" toggle) → load balancing; unassigned after 15 min (emergency) / 4 h (severity 3) / 24 h (severity 2) → escalate to supervisor and notify admin.
Workers see: canonical French summary, original transcript, audio playback, media, protocol path taken, severity reasons, citizen contact and consent status, prior cases.
Worker actions: acknowledge, call citizen (click-to-call via IVR bridge), add note (voice or text), override AI severity (with reason — mandatory), set outcome, schedule follow-up, close.
rows.note: Acknowledge, note, override, outcome, follow-up, and a bridged call that puts the worker on the phone without giving them the number.

rows.requirement: Overrides feed the learning loop (ai.override.recorded) and the Admin dashboard's override rate.
SLA timers are Kafka-scheduled; breaches emit case.sla.breached and notify.
rows.note: SLA timers run in the scheduler rather than on Kafka; the behaviour is the same and the deviation is recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

rows.requirement: Follow-up outcomes ("went to clinic", "child recovered", "sprayed neem", "quiz passed") are captured from the citizen by voice/SMS at scheduled intervals and attached to the case.

Every item in the brief's autosave list is an event (§11) persisted before the response is returned to the channel (write-ahead: event → ack → reply). If persistence fails, the reply is still delivered but flagged and retried; a reply is never lost because logging failed.
Drafts (worker notes, admin prompt edits, report filters) autosave client-side every 2 s to IndexedDB and server-side every 10 s or on blur.
Failed attempts (STT failure, timeout, provider error) and abandoned sessions (no input for 5 min IVR / 24 h WhatsApp) are recorded with reason codes.
Version history: prompts, protocols, glossaries, KB documents and notification templates are immutable versions with approver, diff and rollback.
Every saved record carries: timestamp, actor ID and role, language, module, channel, geo (where available), original input reference, AI interpretation, output, confidence, version, audit status.
Audit log is tamper-evident: hash chain per tenant per day; daily digest exported to cold storage.

Scheduled reports: daily usage; weekly health trends; weekly agri risk; weekly education support; monthly regional activity; monthly NGO impact; quarterly Government programme report; monthly AI performance; monthly cost & usage.
Formats: PDF (branded template), XLSX, CSV, dashboard link. Generated asynchronously; delivered by email/WhatsApp link with expiry.
Report definitions are configurable (filters, scope, cadence) by org admins.
Channels: SMS, WhatsApp (template messages), in-app/push (PWA), email (admin/worker), voice call (IVR outbound for emergencies and reminders to non-WhatsApp users).
Template catalogue with per-language variants, placeholders and approval status (WhatsApp templates require Meta approval — lead time is a dependency).
Types: emergency alert (worker), case assigned, SLA breach, follow-up due, citizen reminder (vaccination, ANC, planting, revision), cluster alert, broadcast (org-scoped, consent-gated), report ready.
Delivery policy: retry with backoff; channel fallback (WhatsApp → SMS → voice); quiet hours 21:00–06:00 local except emergencies; per-citizen frequency cap (≤ 3 non-emergency per week).
Every notification produces delivery events; dashboards show delivery rates per channel/MNO.
Data classification: Class A (identifiable health/pregnancy data, child data), Class B (identifiable non-health), Class C (pseudonymised), Class D (aggregated/anonymised). Controls scale by class.
Workers/admins: OIDC (Google Workspace or Keycloak — [DECISION REQUIRED]), MFA mandatory for admin and supervisor roles, device-bound sessions on the worker PWA.
rows.note: MFA is mandatory for privileged roles, and staff may federate through OIDC with every token claim verified.

rows.requirement: RBAC + ABAC: roles (citizen, chw, nurse, extension_officer, teacher, org_analyst, org_admin, gov_admin, platform_admin, auditor) × attributes (province, territory, org, module). Enforced in BFF and Postgres RLS.
rows.note: Enforced in the API wrapper. Row-level security in PostgreSQL is not used; the deviation is recorded in docs/SECURITY.md.

rows.requirement: Citizens authenticate by channel identity (phone/WhatsApp) + voice OTP for identifier merges and for accessing prior health records via PWA.
rows.note: A spoken one-time code, hashed at rest, ten-minute life, three attempts, before a new identifier joins an existing citizen.

rows.requirement: Encryption in transit (TLS 1.3, mTLS between services); at rest (CMEK via Cloud KMS for Cloud SQL, GCS, Kafka); field-level encryption for Class A columns with per-tenant keys.
rows.note: AES-256-GCM with per-purpose derived keys over second-factor seeds, stored media and phone numbers, with a keyed blind index so an encrypted number is still findable. Customer-managed keys and service-to-service mutual TLS are configured at the platform that hosts this.

rows.requirement: Audio/media: GCS with signed URLs (≤ 15 min), bucket-level retention: raw audio 90 days (configurable), transcripts per retention policy, media for agri 12 months.
rows.note: Media encrypted at rest, served through the application, and swept on its own schedule — 90 days for voice, 365 for images and documents — bytes before rows, with legal holds respected and the sweep audited.

rows.requirement: Pseudonymisation at the analytics boundary: BigQuery receives citizen_pseudo_id (HMAC) and no phone numbers; re-identification requires a two-person approval workflow logged in audit.

Turn object: {turn_id, seq, transcript_raw, lang_detected, lang_confidence, module, domain_result, risk, response:{text_fr, text_user, audio_url}, confidence_overall, escalation, acu} — note: domain_result.citations and model_route are omitted for citizen-facing clients (SEC-08).
rows.note: No provider name reaches a client; tested adversarially.

rows.requirement: Consent management: purpose-based consents (service, reminders, research/model training, sharing with org partners), captured by voice (recorded consent phrase + timestamp) or button; revocable via any channel; enforced at query time.
Children: education profiles for < 18 collect no surname, no school ID unless via a school-tenant agreement; parental consent path for reminders.
Right-to-access/erasure workflow (voice-initiated), 30-day SLA, cascading to derived data except statutory audit.

Security operations: Cloud Armor WAF, DDoS protection, dependency scanning (Snyk/Dependabot), SAST in CI, container image signing, quarterly penetration test, incident response runbook with 72 h breach notification.
rows.note: Dependency audit and static analysis run in CI on every change. A web application firewall, image signing and a quarterly penetration test are bought and operated around a deployment, not committed to a repository.

rows.requirement: IVR: first spoken reply ≤ 6 s after end of citizen utterance (p95); partial TTS streaming permitted
rows.note: Measured per turn and reported as a p95 against the objective; the figure itself needs a real telephony trunk.

rows.requirement: WhatsApp voice note ≤ 30 s audio: reply ≤ 12 s (p95)
rows.note: Measured per turn and reported as a p95 against the objective; the figure itself needs real WhatsApp traffic.

rows.requirement: Photo analysis: ≤ 15 s (p95)
rows.note: Measured per turn and reported as a p95 against the objective; the figure itself needs real photographs at field bandwidth.

rows.requirement: Dashboard page load ≤ 2.5 s (p95) on 3G; API p95 ≤ 400 ms excluding AI calls
rows.note: Page load measured against a throttled 3G profile on a real browser; the run fails if a page misses the objective.

rows.requirement: Throughput baseline: 50 concurrent IVR calls, 500 WhatsApp turns/min at MVP; horizontal scale to 1,000 calls / 10,000 turns/min by Phase 5
rows.note: Concurrent call and turn throughput has not been load-tested against the stated profile.

rows.requirement: 99.5% monthly availability for citizen channels in MVP; 99.9% by Phase 5. Emergency script path 99.95% (served from cached, human-recorded audio even if AI is down).
rows.note: The emergency path is constants and, once recorded, a file. The availability percentage itself is a hosting property.

rows.requirement: RPO 15 min, RTO 2 h (Cloud SQL HA + PITR; Kafka replication factor 3).
rows.note: Recovery point and recovery time come from the database configuration and a restore exercise.

rows.requirement: Circuit breakers per AI provider; automatic failover per routing table.
rows.note: Per-provider failover along the configured chain.

rows.requirement: Target cost per completed interaction ≤ USD 0.08 blended (AI + infra) at 100k interactions/month; ≤ USD 0.04 at 1M/month — excluding telephony/WhatsApp fees, which are reported separately.
rows.note: Cost per completed interaction is metered per turn. Whether it lands under the target depends on provider pricing and volume.

rows.requirement: ACU metering accurate to ±2% versus provider invoices.
rows.note: Every AI call is metered against a versioned conversion table and attributed. Reconciling that table against a provider invoice requires an invoice, which requires a signed contract.

rows.requirement: Worker/admin UIs WCAG 2.2 AA; RTL not required; all UI strings i18n (fr primary, en admin optional).
rows.note: WCAG 2.2 A/AA checked by axe-core on every worker and admin page, zero violations, and all UI strings in the five languages. An audit with assistive-technology users is fieldwork.

rows.requirement: Citizen voice UX tested with ≥ 30 low-literacy users per pilot province before launch (task success ≥ 80%).
rows.note: Thirty low-literacy users per pilot province, tested before launch. Not something a repository can contain.

rows.requirement: OpenTelemetry traces across adapter → session → agent → gateway; per-turn trace ID surfaced in admin UI.
rows.note: Every request carries a trace id end to end and the OpenTelemetry SDK exports spans when an endpoint is configured.

rows.requirement: SLO dashboards (latency, availability, STT WER drift, low-confidence rate, SLA breach rate, cost) with paging via on-call rota.
rows.note: Every objective is measured and reported, with breaching separated from unmeasured so an absent signal is never read as a met target. Paging and an on-call rota are staffed around a deployment.

rows.requirement: FDSU/Government is the paying tenant; Nseya provides the technology; pricing is platform licence + per-ACU consumption + telephony/WhatsApp pass-through — [DECISION REQUIRED] commercial terms.
rows.note: Licence and per-unit pricing are commercial terms between the programme and its supplier.

rows.requirement: ACU definition (portfolio standard): 1 ACU = normalised unit across STT seconds, TTS characters, LLM tokens, vision calls, using a published conversion table versioned in admin-config.

Every cvos.metering.acu event is attributed to tenant/org/module/language/channel; monthly statement generated by the reporting service; invoicing and settlement via BitriPay institutional rails; no citizen is ever charged.
rows.note: Every metering event is attributed to tenant, organisation, module, language and channel, and monthly statements are generated. Settlement through a named payment provider needs a commercial agreement with that provider.

rows.requirement: Budget guardrails: per-tenant monthly ACU cap with 80/95/100% alerts; at cap, non-emergency AI features degrade to scripted mode rather than stop.
rows.note: At the cap, non-emergency AI degrades to scripted rather than stopping.

rows.requirement: Monorepo (Turborepo/pnpm) for TypeScript services and PWA; separate Python repo for agent-runtime; shared @cvos/contracts package (OpenAPI types, event schemas, DomainResult) published from schema sources.
rows.note: One application rather than the proposed monorepo split. A national platform maintained by a small team pays the coordination cost of a split repository long before it gets the benefit; the reasoning is recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

rows.requirement: Environments: dev (ephemeral per PR preview for PWA), staging (full stack, synthetic data, sandbox telephony/WhatsApp), prod. IaC via Terraform; GitOps via Argo CD.
rows.note: Environments are declared as Terraform in this repository, with a container image that runs the same way in each.

rows.requirement: CI: lint, typecheck, unit (≥ 80% on core services), contract tests (Pact) between adapters and session, integration tests with Testcontainers (Postgres, Kafka), AI eval suite (gold sets + red team) on prompt/model changes, e2e (Playwright) for PWA and admin.
Release: trunk-based; feature flags for modules/languages/channels per province; canary 5% → 25% → 100%; rollback ≤ 10 min.
rows.note: Trunk-based with a green gate, feature flags scoped by province, role and module, and canaries that start at 5 % and are held seven days.

rows.requirement: Data migrations: Prisma/Flyway with backward-compatible expand/contract; event schema evolution with Schema Registry compatibility = BACKWARD.
rows.note: Migrations are generated, checked for destructive statements before they can merge, and applied at boot. The second half of the requirement assumes an event bus with a schema registry; this platform has no event bus, so there is no registry to keep backward-compatible.

rows.requirement: Synthetic data generator for all five languages for staging and demos (no real citizen data outside prod).
rows.note: Synthetic data in five languages, refused in production.
